howto.name: Upload a video
howto.text: MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, MKV — up to 500 MB.

howto.name: Choose target format
howto.text: MP4 (universal), WebM (open, smaller), MOV (Apple), AVI (legacy), MKV (open container).

howto.name: Download the converted video
howto.text: FFmpeg transcodes via the appropriate codec (H.264 for MP4, VP9/Opus for WebM, etc.).

faq.a: MP4: most compatible. WebM: smaller, used for web embedding. MOV: works in Apple ecosystem and Final Cut. MKV: open-source flexible container.

Every output is re-encoded, so a small loss is normal. MP4, MOV and MKV use H.264 at CRF 23, WebM uses VP9 at about 1 Mbit/s, and AVI uses MPEG-4 with MP3 audio. None of the outputs is lossless, MKV included.
It depends on the length, the resolution and the format. A conversion that runs longer than three minutes is stopped, so trim or resize long videos first.

faq.q: Does the converted video keep where it was recorded?
faq.a: No. The location (GPS), the make, model and software of the phone or camera, the recording date, and tags such as the title and comments are left out, whatever the format. What the video needs to play as recorded is kept: a clip a phone stored sideways comes out upright, the sound track keeps its language, and so does a subtitle track carried into an MKV or WebM. Chapter markers keep their place and titles. AVI has no place for languages or chapters.
